([[def-compactly-supported-differential-form]]).
associated_step_blocks: 2.1 Since $\overline{P_k}$ is compact and contained in $P_{k+1}$, apply [F6] to obtain a smooth $\chi$ equal to $1$ near $\overline{P_k}$ with $\operatorname{supp}\chi\subset P_{k+1}$. fact_or_definition_blocks: [F1] [[def-compactly-supported-differential-form]]: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, and $k\geq0$. For $\omega\in\Omega^k(M)$ define $$\operatorname{supp}\omega=\overline{\{p\in M:\omega_p\neq0\}}^{\,M},\qquad \Omega_c^k(M)=\{\omega\in\Omega^k(M):\operatorname{supp}\omega\text{ is compact}\}.$$ The closure and compactness are in $M$, including its genuine boundary. Zero is the intrinsic zero of each exterior-power fiber, so this definition is independent of trivialization. The zero form has empty support.

associated_step_blocks: 1.1 The support convention [F1] for functions, regarded as zero-forms, gives $f=0$ on $U\setminus K$. By [F3], $K$ is compact and closed in $\mathbb R^n$. Continuity from [F2] makes the sets $\{x\in K:|f(x)|<j\}$, for positive integers $j$, an open cover of $K$. A finite subcover bounds $|f|$ on $K$, hence bounds $\widetilde f$ everywhere. Off $K$, the extension is locally zero. At a point of $U$ with $x_n>0$, relative openness supplies a Euclidean neighbourhood contained in $U$, on which the extension is smooth by [F2]. Points with $x_n<0$ are outside $K$. Thus $\widetilde f$ is smooth away from the genuine face, and its support lies in the closed compact set $K$. Empty $K$ gives the identically zero function. [F1, F2, F3]

fact_or_definition_blocks: [L2] For a nonempty box $B=B(a,b)$ and strictly increasing lists $a_i = c_{i,0} < \dots < c_{i,N_i} = b_i$ with $N_i \ge 1$, the cells $Q_k$ are nonempty pairwise disjoint boxes with union $B$ and $\operatorname{vol}(B) = \sum_{k_0<N_0}\cdots\sum_{k_{n-1}<N_{n-1}}\operatorname{vol}(Q_k)$ ([[lem-box-volume-is-additive-over-grid-subdivisions]]).
associated_step_blocks: 2.1 For each $j<m$ let $w^j_k := \operatorname{vol}(Q_k)$ when $Q_k \subseteq B_j$ and $w^j_k := 0$ otherwise; then $\operatorname{vol}(B_j) = \sum_{k_0<N_0}\cdots\sum_{k_{n-1}<N_{n-1}} w^j_k$, because for $B_j = \varnothing$ no cell is contained in it and both sides are $0$, while for $B_j = B(a^j,b^j)$ nonempty the parameters $a^j_i$ and $b^j_i$ occur among the grid points, say $a^j_i = c_{i,\alpha_i}$ and $b^j_i = c_{i,\beta_i}$ with $\alpha_i<\beta_i$, the cells contained in $B_j$ are exactly those with $\alpha_i \le k_i < \beta_i$ in every coordinate, the lists $c_{i,\alpha_i}<\dots<c_{i,\beta_i}$ subdivide $B_j$ so that [L2] applies, and widening each summation range from $\alpha_i \le k_i < \beta_i$ to $k_i<N_i$ only inserts zero terms. [step 1.1, step 1.2, L2, L3, F1]

fact_or_definition_blocks: [L1] The algebraic quotient universal property gives a unique linear map $\overline T:X/M\to Y$ with $\overline T(qx)=Tx$ ([[thm-quotient-vector-space-universal-property]]).

fact_or_definition_blocks: [L2] Similar matrices are exactly matrix representations of one endomorphism in different ordered bases ([[thm-similarity-is-an-equivalence-relation-and-models-basis-change]]).
associated_step_blocks: 3.1 If $B=P^{-1}AP$, induction gives $B^k=P^{-1}A^kP$, and therefore $p(B)=P^{-1}p(A)P$. Thus $p(B)=0$ exactly when $p(A)=0$, so [L3] again gives $\mu_B=\mu_A$. This also follows from [L2]. [L2, L3, algebra] ∎
